title: Cameroon Koki Corn (Steamed Fresh-Corn Cake)
author: Abi Olayiwola (Eat Well Abi)
desc: Fresh corn and onion blended coarsely and mixed with corn flour, palm oil and spinach, then steamed about an hour on a bed of corn husks until the cake holds together.
longDesc: A fresh-corn koki: four ears of corn and an onion are blended coarsely with about a quarter cup of water. The pot is lined with corn husks and the mixture steamed around an hour — the page says to check after 15–20 minutes that the water has not dried out — then rested 10 minutes. The cue given is that the cake should hold together and not fall apart, and it firms up as it cools. A second printing (Adamu, 24 Nov 2012) uses 5 ears of corn, 1 cup cornmeal and 3 cups of spinach and says the dish is made predominantly in Cameroon during the rainy season; its steam time differs between its article and its recipe card.
steps: Blend the corn and onion coarsely with about a quarter cup of water.
Mix in the corn flour, palm oil, salt and chopped spinach.
Line the pot with corn husks, add the mixture and steam for about 1 hour. Check after 15–20 minutes that the water has not dried out.
Rest 10 minutes. The cake should hold together and not fall apart; it firms up as it cools.
chefTips: The printed cue is that the koki ‘should hold together and not fall apart’ (single-pass).
Check the steamer water after 15–20 minutes.
Leave it to firm up as it cools.
commonMistakes: Blending the corn to a fine puree — the page says coarse.
Cutting it hot, before the rest.
healthBenefits: Fresh corn gives fibre and starch; spinach adds greens.
culturalNote: The page calls it a traditional Cameroon dish prepared with fresh corn ground and steamed. The second printing says it is made predominantly in Cameroon during the rainy season.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Cameroon Koki Corn’. Byline as printed: ‘Abi Olayiwola’. Published Mar 22, 2022; modified Dec 7, 2022. Yield 4. Prep 45 min, cook 1 h. Ingredients TWO-PASS; the ‘should hold together’ cue is SINGLE-PASS. The exact wording of the mixing step was not captured verbatim; the mixing line above follows the ingredient list.

Second printing (not used for quantities): Adamu, ‘Koki Corn’, 24 Nov 2012 (updated 11 Feb 2025), 5 ears corn, 1 cup cornmeal, 3 cups spinach, 1 teaspoon salt, 2–3 tablespoons palm oil; article says steam about 30 minutes, the recipe card prints ‘about an hour minutes’ (typo), her reply says an hour. Recorded, not reconciled.
ABSENT: the water quantity for the steamer; salt quantity.
